A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same SCOPE paper, including all 25 pages and Appendices A.1–A.13. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish identical scientific content. The only visible difference is the first-page arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original SCOPE experiments on simulated conversations, including reward comparisons, ablations, runtime measurements, and DailyDialog evaluation results (Section 6 and appendices).

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including Figures 3–5 and the appendix results in Tables 1, 2, and 4–7.

M1.justification: Sections 4–5, Algorithm 1, and Appendices A.4/A.6 retain identical semantic-space MCTS procedures, transition and reward models, training losses, and response-selection steps.

E1.justification: Both versions use LMSYS-Chat-1M and DailyDialog conversation data and evaluate harmfulness and human-response length. The DailyDialog generalization scenario in Appendix A.13 is unchanged.

E2.justification: Random, 0-step Greedy, 1-step Greedy, and vanilla MCTS remain the main comparators. Corresponding ablation and appendix comparisons retain the same comparator membership.

E3.justification: Section 6.2 and Appendix A.11 retain the same five-turn evaluation, 100 conversation starters per dataset, model roles, reward metrics, planning budgets, discount factor 0.9, and branching factor 5.

E4.justification: The transition-model and search-depth ablations in Figure 5, engagement-proxy analysis in Table 1, transition-prediction analyses in Appendix A.8, and qualitative cases in Appendix A.12 are identical.

E5.justification: Appendices A.6/A.11 retain the same training seeds, five evaluation trials, and generation-seeding instructions. Error bars and tabulated uncertainty reporting are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical results, plotted trends, and qualitative examples match. For example, Table 2 retains rollout times of 0.18 ± 0.028 seconds for SCOPE and 16.63 ± 10.98 seconds for vanilla MCTS; Tables 6–7 retain identical DailyDialog results.

T1.justification: The MDP definitions, Proposition A.1 and its assumptions and proof in Appendix A.3, and the reward/transition-model derivations are identical.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that SCOPE plans in semantic space without additional LLM simulation queries, achieves higher cumulative rewards under practical budgets, and plans 70 times faster than conventional simulation-based planning.

C2.justification: Interpretations of efficiency, transition-model errors, and engagement remain unchanged. Both retain the limitations concerning fixed transition models and discussion of adapting them to specific LLMs or users.

D1.justification: The reproducibility statement and Appendices A.6/A.11 retain identical code-access information, model specifications, prompts, preprocessing, hyperparameters, hardware, and training-time details.

R1.justification: The references and positioning against myopic response selection, fine-tuning, LLM-based simulation, and state abstraction are unchanged. No cited research is added or removed.

P1.justification: The first-page margin stamp changes from arXiv v1, 14 March 2025, to v2, 7 June 2025. The displayed title, authors, prose, headings, and main-text/appendix structure remain identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–11, Tables 1–7, captions, axes, legends, and placement are unchanged. Pages 2–25 render identically; the first-page stamp update does not alter the paper's layout.

improvement.justification: The methods, empirical evidence, theory, limitations, and reproducibility documentation are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. The administrative version/date update does not materially improve or worsen the paper's scientific or expository quality.
